evaluator: Blind Stagebench Phase 1 evaluator; measured the published build served on 127.0.0.1:5421 in a real Chrome via Playwright, with an AnalyserNode spliced onto every node connecting to AudioDestinationNode, a stubbed navigator.requestMIDIAccess, CDP multi-touch, and document.elementFromPoint hit-testing.
summary: A disciplined, unusually honest Phase 1. The build renders the full Stage 4 73 surface (146 stable control IDs, 7/24/14/28/40/33 per section, only Program and Synth OLEDs) and 73 contiguous keys E1-E7 (43 white / 30 black, black-key height fraction 0.610). The piano voice is real live synthesis: fundamental plus two inharmonic partials measured on rendered spectra across E1-E7, natural exponential decay (RMS 0.360 to 0.0035 over 5.9 s), ~135 ms key release vs ~250 ms pedal release, and velocity spanning peak 0.026 to 0.916. Pointer, independent multi-touch, computer keyboard with repeat suppression, and Web MIDI (note/velocity/CC64/CC123) all drive one lifecycle; blur and MIDI disconnect return output to exact digital silence; voice stealing is deterministic and audible. Honesty is exemplary: exactly one GainNode reaches the destination, zeroing it silences everything, operating all 146 controls yields 0.0 RMS, and no audio or image assets ship. Two real defects: no gain headroom (a two-note chord at velocity 100 already peaks at 1.16, so the destination hard-clips), and the Layer Effects section is overcrowded enough that two buttons are 0/25 pointer-reachable.

evidence: Pitch is correct across the whole keybed, measured on rendered spectra via getFloatFrequencyData (fftSize 2048, 48 kHz, 23.4 Hz bins): E1 peak 46.9 Hz vs 41.2 expected, E2 93.8 vs 82.4, C4 257.8 vs 261.6, C5 515.6 vs 523.3, E7 2648.4 vs 2637.0 - every one inside one bin.

C4 shows three partials at 257.8 / 515.6 / 796.9 Hz (-21.1 / -31.4 / -46.5 dB), matching the declared fundamental plus 2.0027x and 3.0142x stretched partials, with the upper ones lower and faster-decaying.

Held C4 at velocity 110 decays smoothly and naturally: analyser RMS 0.360 at t=200 ms, 0.152 at 1.2 s, 0.0406 at 2.8 s, 0.0107 at 4.4 s, 0.0035 at 5.9 s - a plausible piano decay envelope, and low notes ring measurably longer than high ones (E7 RMS 0.222 vs E1 0.335 at the same velocity).

Release behaves: after note-off, RMS falls 0.304 -> 0.0009 in 135 ms and reaches exactly 0 by 216 ms; with sustain held the same note keeps its natural decay (0.331 -> 0.104 over 1.37 s) and only releases when the pedal lifts, over a longer ~250 ms tail.

Velocity mapping is monotonic and wide: single C4 peaks 0.0256 (vel 10), 0.128 (40), 0.384 (80), 0.857 (127) - roughly 30 dB of dynamic range, with the filter cutoff audibly opening on harder strikes.

Defect: there is no headroom. Measured peak at the node feeding AudioDestinationNode is 0.916 for a single note at vel 127, 1.158 for a two-note chord at vel 100, 1.598 for three notes, 2.560 for five and 3.385 for ten (+10.6 dBFS). Anything above unity is hard-clipped by the destination, so ordinary chords played at mezzo-forte or above distort.

The voice is a simple three-oscillator additive tone plus a 90 ms noise transient - recognisably synthetic and lacking sympathetic resonance or release detail, a simplification a knowledgeable player would notice (Phase 1 explicitly permits honest synthesis).

Verified by instrumenting AudioNode.prototype.connect in the running build: exactly one node ever connects to AudioDestinationNode (["GainNode"]), and forcing that gain to 0 while 24 notes sound drops analyser RMS from 1.858 to 0.000000 - nothing bypasses the master gain, exactly as IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json claims.

The declared synthesis matches the rendered signal: measured partial ratios and the hammer-noise attack correspond to the declared OscillatorNode set and the seeded 90 ms AudioBuffer (src/audio/pianoVoice.ts, scheduled in src/audio/pianoEngine.ts:131-159); no decodeAudioData call and no data:audio URI exists anywhere in build/assets/index-Q8iAhm8P.js.

The 'no audio files of any kind' claim holds: the published build is two assets (282 KB JS, 20 KB CSS) and the only network request beyond them is a 404 on /favicon.ico. No media file of any type ships in the artifact outside evidence/.

The claim that all 146 panel controls are connected to no audio node is asserted, not just stated: driving every control in the inventory in the live build produced a maximum analyser RMS of 0.00000000, and every control carries data-functional="false" in the DOM (146/146).

IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json notes[2] is candid that the tests substitute the candidate's own deterministic offline Web Audio renderer (src/audio/offline.ts) rather than a browser engine - it does not overclaim browser-verified audio.

Pointer: mouse-down on the C4 key element (button#key-60, aria-label "C4, MIDI note 60") drove the AudioContext from state 'idle' to 'ready' and produced peak 0.694 / RMS 0.116; mouse-up returned output to 0. Dragging off the keybed keeps the note held (pointer capture) and releasing anywhere ends it; dragging C4 -> E4 transfers the held note (glissando).

Independent multi-touch verified with raw CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent: two simultaneous touch points left data-held="true" on both C4 and E4 with RMS 0.543, and lifting one finger left exactly ["E4"] still held.

Computer keyboard maps chromatically from C4 (a->C4, w->C#4, s->D4, e->D#4, d->E4, f->F4, t->F#4, g->G4, y->G#4, h->A4, u->A#4, j->B4, k->C5, o->C#5, l->D5, p->D#5); Z shifts down an octave (a then plays C3) and Space holds sustain (the on-screen button text flips to "Sustain pedal (down)").
Repeat suppression works: five synthetic keydown events with repeat:true after the initial press left the OLED readout at VOICES 01 rather than retriggering.

Web MIDI through a stubbed navigator.requestMIDIAccess: note-on/note-off, velocity, CC64 sustain and CC123 all-notes-off all reach the same lifecycle (CC123 dropped RMS 0.615 -> 0). Enter or Space on a focused key also presses it (E4 held, RMS 0.317).

Failure paths are honest, not silent: a rejected requestMIDIAccess renders data-midi-permission="denied" with "MIDI access was denied. (Permission denied)" while the keybed still sounds (RMS 0.124); removing navigator.requestMIDIAccess renders "unsupported"; removing window.AudioContext renders "Web Audio is not available in this browser - the keybed responds but stays silent" with zero page errors.
Velocity moves level in the expected direction across four measured points (peak 0.0256 / 0.128 / 0.384 / 0.857 for MIDI velocities 10 / 40 / 80 / 127).

Sustain transitions are correct on rendered signal: with CC64 down, note-off leaves the note decaying naturally for 1.37 s; CC64 up then releases it over ~250 ms, measurably longer than the ~135 ms key release.

Voice stealing is deterministic and audible. Holding low E1 (MIDI 36) and then adding 34 further distinct notes and releasing them left RMS 0.000 - the oldest voice had been stolen at the 32-voice cap. Repeating with only 12 further notes (cap not exceeded) left the low note still sounding at RMS 0.297.

All-notes-off is real: three sounding notes at RMS 0.489 fell to 0.000 with every data-held cleared on a window blur event, and two sounding notes at RMS 0.406 fell to 0.000 on a MIDI statechange disconnect.
Cleanup returns to exact digital silence rather than a residual floor - repeated measurements after releases read RMS 0.00000, and the OLED voice readout returned to VOICES 00.

Blemish: the OLED 'VOICES' readout is fed by instrument.heldNotes.size (src/App.tsx:40), not the engine's voice count, so it showed VOICES 34 against a 32-voice cap, and read VOICES 01 for a stolen, silent voice.

145 of 146 controls change their exposed state under keyboard operation or a click; the remaining one (perf.pitch-stick) responds to a real pointer drag, going aria-valuenow 0 -> 0.5 during the drag and springing back to 0 on release, which is correct hardware behaviour.

Momentary buttons behave like momentary hardware: program.store, program.slot.3, organ.octave-up and synth.sound-init all gain data-pressed="true" during a held mouse-down and drop it on release, rather than latching.

The decorative boundary is honest and measurable: driving every one of the 146 controls produced a maximum analyser RMS of 0.00000000, and driving perf.master-level from 7.5 down to 3.5 while a note sounded did not change the rendered level (RMS 0.389 -> 0.368, consistent with decay alone).
The panel says so on its own face - the Program OLED reads "PANEL CONTROLS: DECORATIVE" and "PIANO: GENERATED VOICE", and every control carries data-functional="false" in the DOM.

Accessibility holds: 0/146 controls lack an accessible name, 0/146 are unfocusable, roles are real (44 slider, 5 spinbutton, 3 status, 1 group) with aria-valuenow/valuetext, and a focused drawbar shows a 2px solid rgb(63,169,255) outline.

Defect: two controls cannot be pressed with a pointer at all. A 5x5 document.elementFromPoint grid at 1440x900, page unscrolled, resolves 0/25 points to fx.mod1.on and 0/25 to fx.mod2.on; six more FX controls score 10/25 or worse (fx.delay.on 2/25, fx.reverb.on 4/25, fx.amp.type 5/25, fx.delay.tap 5/25), and a real mouse click at the centre of fx.reverb.on and fx.delay.on lands on DIV.chassis__cheek instead, leaving aria-pressed unchanged.

All six sections are present in order with 146 stable, namespaced control IDs distributed 7 perf / 24 organ / 14 piano / 28 program / 40 synth / 33 fx, exactly matching the inventory declared in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json and the visual audit.

Program and Synth are the only primary OLEDs (data-oled resolves to exactly ["program","synth"]), and the required landmark families are all on the panel: 9 organ drawbars, vib/chorus and B3 percussion, rotary speaker, morph assign, program slots 1-8, synth oscillator/filter/amp/LFO/arp, and six effect units plus Rotary.
The chassis is continuous and nothing overflows it: measured chassis rect 1368x442 at 1440x900 with 0 controls falling outside its bounds, and all 73 keys hit-test reachable (73/73).

Defect: the Layer Effects section is overcrowded to the point of illegibility. A 1120x50 300x200 crop shows controls overlapping their neighbours, the REVERB type column clipped at the right edge ("ROOM / BRIGHT / BOOTH" and "VAR | CHOR" cut mid-word), and 23 of the 33 fx controls have at least one occluded hit-test grid point.

Silkscreen legends render at roughly 4 px at desktop size and read as grey micro-texture rather than words, so several controls are only identifiable through their accessible names - a deviation the candidate declares openly in evidence/stage1-visual-audit.md section 6.1 rather than hiding.

All 11 Phase 1 feature IDs appear in tests/feature-matrix.json mapped to real, non-empty test files, and inputs/verification.json records coveredFeatures 11 / requiredFeatures 11 with test, typecheck, lint and build all passing.

I exercised each ID against the running build rather than trusting the matrix. visual.key-count: 73 keys, MIDI 28-100 contiguous, 43 white / 30 black, lowest E1, highest E7, black-key height fraction 0.6100 and black/white width ratio 0.6499. visual.control-inventory: 146 IDs, two OLEDs. interaction.keys: press, release, cancel, glissando and multi-touch all confirmed.

piano.basic-note-lifecycle, basic-inputs, basic-sustain-polyphony and basic-status-cleanup were each confirmed live (see the sound and playability evidence): rendered signal above silence, three input paths, CC64 sustain, deterministic stealing at the 32-voice cap, and a return to RMS 0.000 on blur, disconnect and all-notes-off.

piano.basic-status-cleanup reports only states that can really occur - idle, ready, unsupported, denied - with no invented loading progress, verified by removing window.AudioContext and navigator.requestMIDIAccess and observing the honest fallback copy.
regression.chassis holds at both required viewports: nothing clipped at 1440x900, and at 390x844 the complete instrument is present, unclipped and accompanied by a Zoom control in the status strip.

Every gap claim I tested held. 'All 146 panel controls are decorative' - confirmed by 0.00000000 RMS while operating all of them and data-functional="false" on 146/146. 'Counts by section: performance 7, organ 24, piano 14, program 28, synth 40, effects 33' - the DOM returns exactly {perf:7, organ:24, piano:14, program:28, synth:40, fx:33}.

'Only the keybed and the sustain input produce sound' - confirmed: Master Level driven 7.5 -> 3.5 with a note sounding left the rendered level unchanged, while the keybed, Space, the on-screen sustain button and MIDI CC64 all reached the audio graph.

Nothing undeclared was found missing: the six piano types, KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Timbre, Unison, Soft Release, String Res, layers, octave shift, the organ and synth engines, the effect units, programs, splits, scenes and morphs are all explicitly listed as Phase 1 non-goals in evidence/stage1-visual-audit.md section 7, and all of them are indeed inert.

The OLEDs refuse to fabricate state - the Program OLED shows only live engine/panel/MIDI status and the Synth OLED says the engine is not implemented, matching declared deviations 7 and 8 rather than showing a fake program name.

The audit goes beyond the minimum by flagging a contradiction between prompts/stage1.md's stale section fractions and specs/nord-stage-4.visual.json v1.2.0, re-measuring the reference photo itself, and declaring which source it followed.

Two small inaccuracies: the MIDI status still reads "MIDI connected. (Stagebench Test Input)" after a device disconnects, because inputNamesOf (src/input/midi.ts:97-103) does not filter ports by state, and the OLED VOICES readout counts held note IDs rather than live voices.

issues.title: No gain headroom - ordinary chords hard-clip at the destination
issues.detail: Measured on the node feeding AudioDestinationNode with a spliced AnalyserNode: a single C4 at velocity 127 already peaks at 0.916, a two-note chord at velocity 100 peaks at 1.158, three notes 1.598, five notes 2.560, ten notes 3.385 (+10.6 dBFS) and 24 notes RMS 1.858. AudioDestinationNode clamps to [-1,1], so any chord played above roughly mezzo-forte is hard-clipped and distorts. Per-voice gain is set from velocity with no polyphony-aware normalisation or limiter ahead of the 0.7 master gain (src/audio/pianoEngine.ts:127, master.gain.value = 0.7 at line 68).

issues.title: Two Layer Effects buttons are unreachable by pointer
issues.detail: A 5x5 document.elementFromPoint grid at 1440x900 with the page unscrolled resolves 0 of 25 points to fx.mod1.on and 0 of 25 to fx.mod2.on - they are entirely covered by neighbouring controls (a real click at fx.mod1.on's centre lands on SPAN.knob#fx.delay.tempo). fx.delay.on (2/25), fx.reverb.on (4/25), fx.amp.type (5/25) and fx.delay.tap (5/25) are nearly as bad, with their centres landing on DIV.chassis__cheek. A mouse user cannot press these controls at all; only keyboard users can, which conflicts with the Phase 1 gate that every visible panel control presses accessibly.

issues.title: Layer Effects section is overcrowded and clipped at the right edge
issues.detail: In a crop of the rendered build at x 1120-1420, y 50-250, the Delay and Reverb columns overlap their neighbours and their legends are cut mid-word ("ROOM / BRIGHT / BOOTH", "VAR | CHOR"). 23 of the 33 fx controls have at least one occluded hit-test grid point. The section's controls exist and carry correct accessible names, but several are not visually identifiable.

issues.title: OLED VOICES readout counts held note IDs, not live voices
issues.detail: src/App.tsx:40 feeds the readout from instrument.heldNotes.size. With the engine capped at 32 voices, sending 34 note-ons displayed "VOICES 34", and after a voice was deterministically stolen the display still read "VOICES 01" for a voice that had been destroyed and was silent. The underlying stealing behaviour is correct; only the report is wrong.

issues.title: MIDI status still reports a disconnected device as connected
issues.detail: After a MIDIAccess statechange marking the port disconnected, the status region still read "MIDI connected. (Stagebench Test Input)". inputNamesOf (src/input/midi.ts:97-103) lists every port in access.inputs without checking port.state. Voices were correctly stopped on the disconnect, so the behaviour is right and only the message is stale.

issues.title: Audio tests assert on the candidate's own Web Audio simulator, not a browser engine
issues.detail: The suite contains no mocks at all (0 occurrences of vi.fn or vi.mock) and makes 30 assertions against rendered sample data, but that data comes from src/audio/offline.ts - a 438-line hand-written renderer of the Web Audio subset the engine uses, run under jsdom. It really evaluates oscillators, envelopes, buffer playback and the biquad sample by sample, so it is far stronger than mocking, but a divergence between it and Chrome's implementation would go unnoticed. IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json states this openly. My independent browser measurements corroborate the audio claims, and the clipping defect above is exactly the kind of thing an offline renderer with no destination clamp will not surface.
